text: Viettel secures telecommunications licence to enter Dominican Republic market

Viettel Dominicana S.A.S. officially signed a telecommunications concession agreement with the Dominican Republic's Telecommunications Institute (INDOTEL) at the institute's headquarters on November 16, marking the Vietnamese group's formal entry into the country's telecommunications market.
The agreement follows INDOTEL's approval of Viettel's successful bid in an international tender organised by the regulator.
Under the deal, Viettel has been granted the right to use a total of 240 MHz of spectrum across the 700 MHz, 2,300 MHz and C-band frequencies for 4G and 5G mobile networks over a 20-year period.
The spectrum allocation provides the foundation for the company to develop modern mobile and broadband networks in the Caribbean nation.

The project builds on Viettel's investment presence in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Peru and Haiti, as the group pursues its strategy of developing sustainable telecommunications infrastructure.

Viettel Dominicana said it plans to build its network infrastructure and operational capabilities to serve Dominican consumers and businesses over the long term, while complying with local laws and operating under INDOTEL's supervision.
As a new market entrant, the company plans to roll out nationwide 4G and 5G infrastructure, extending coverage beyond urban centres to remote areas.
